stem:
Arnav matches large-number names to powers of $10$. He knows $1$ lakh $=10^{5}$ in the Indian system and $1$ million $=10^{6}$ in the international system.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: $1$ lakh equals $1$ million because both names are large.

teacher.key_rationale: 10^6 / 10^5 = 10, so 1 million = 10 lakh. Setting 1 lakh = 10^6 swaps the power. Setting 1 million = 10^5 drops the given powers. Equating the names because both are large captures surface size language.
